seo.title: ODDference — what can business and society learn from creative expertise?
seo.description: ODDference is a professional event exploring what business and wider society can learn from creative and cultural expertise. Helsinki, 2027.

title: Where creative expertise meets business and society.

concept.headline: What can business and the rest of society learn from creative expertise?
concept.body:
ODDference is a professional event for learning from creative and cultural expertise — and for meeting clients, partners, collaborators and decision-makers outside your usual circuit.

People who work in art, design, music, film, games and media decide every day what deserves attention, what people will remember, and how to make something that did not exist before. Those are useful questions to bring into a business, a city or an institution. ODDference is where that exchange happens in a serious room.

reasonsIntro.headline: Three reasons to be in the room.

reasons.title: Take a different kind of expertise back to work.
reasons.body: ODDference brings creative and cultural practice into questions about leadership, technology, organisations and society. The point is not inspiration for its own sake, but new ways to look at problems you already have.

reasons.title: Meet people worth doing business with.
reasons.body: ODDference deliberately mixes creative leaders, business leaders, founders, policymakers, institutions and researchers, with time built in for the conversations that follow. That puts clients, partners and collaborators in the room who are hard to find at a single-industry conference.

reasons.title: The event should prove its own point.
reasons.body: If ODDference argues that creative expertise matters, the experience cannot stop at the speaker list. Artists and creative practitioners can shape the spaces, scenography, performances, food, music and other parts of how the event feels and behaves.

faq.question: What is ODDference?
faq.answer: A professional event where creative and cultural practitioners take the stage as experts rather than as entertainment, and business leaders, founders, policymakers and institutions come to learn from them. The 2026 edition ran over two days in central Helsinki with 25 speakers and more than 30 sessions.

faq.question: When and where is ODDference 2027?
faq.answer: Helsinki. The exact dates and venues are not confirmed yet — ticket holders hear first as each piece is settled. ODDference takes place alongside the wider ODDfest week across the city.

faq.question: Is the 2027 programme published?
faq.answer: Not yet. Blind Bird is deliberately sold before the programme is complete, which is why it is the lowest price the event will be sold at. The 2026 speakers and sessions above are there so you can judge what the event is actually like before the next line-up exists.

faq.question: Why buy before the programme is announced?
faq.answer: Price. Blind Bird is €299, Early Bird is €399 and the regular ticket is €499, each plus VAT 13.5%, so committing early is worth €200 against the full price. If you would rather wait for the line-up, the later tiers will be there.

faq.question: Can I buy an Early Bird or regular ticket now?
faq.answer: No. One tier is on sale at a time — right now that is Blind Bird. The other two are shown with their real prices so you can see what waiting costs, and they open in turn.

faq.question: Does an ODDference ticket include ODDfest?
faq.answer: ODDference 2027 takes place alongside ODDfest week, and the 2026 ODDference Pass included ODDfest access. What the 2027 ticket includes beyond ODDference itself is not settled yet — the ticket page is the source of truth for what each ticket covers.

faq.question: What language is ODDference in?
faq.answer: ODDference 2026 ran in English, with speakers from Finland, Denmark, Canada and the US.

faq.question: Who is it for?
faq.answer: Business leaders, founders, business development and partnership people, organisational leaders, policymakers and institutions, and creative leaders working beyond the cultural sector. It is built for people who want perspectives and relationships outside their own industry.

faq.question: Can my organisation partner with ODDference?
faq.answer: Yes. Partnerships can be an idea, a question, expertise or resources — the ones that work improve the event for the people in the room rather than adding a logo. Use the partnership link on this page and tell us what you have in mind.
